title: Why Plane Windows Are Never Square
description:
In 1954, two Comet jets, the world's first jet airliners, broke apart in the air within months. To find out why, engineers sank a whole Comet in a giant water tank and pumped it up and down like thousands of flights, until a crack appeared at the sharp corner of a squarish window. Stress piles up at sharp corners. Round corners spread it out, so every airliner window since has rounded corners.

What other shapes around you are hiding a reason?

Sources: FAA Lessons Learned, "de Havilland DH-106 Comet 1"; Aviation Safety Network (Comet G-ALYP, 1954); This Day in Aviation, "Metal Fatigue"; Plane & Pilot magazine.
